original_question: Given a continuous graph Gamma, can one derive informative lower and upper bounds for chi_{1/2}(Gamma), the minimum number of colors in a valid radius-1/2 ball cover, as a function of the chromatic number chi(Gamma's combinatorial counterpart) and the number n of endpoints, or as a function of other polynomial-time computable graph parameters?
target_in_paper: Section 3.3, 'Chromatic number', specifically the open question under 'Approximability and bounds' asking for lower and upper bounds on χ_{1/2}(Γ) in terms of χ(G(Γ)) and n=|V|, with possible alternative bounds via other polynomial-time computable parameters. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.14554))
correct_elements: Your draft already identifies the correct problem type (bounds for the continuous chromatic parameter), the correct fixed radius r=1/2, the dependence on the chromatic number of the corresponding combinatorial graph, the relevance of the number of endpoints n, and the paper's explicit interest in other polynomial-time computable parameters. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.14554))
missing_details: The paper works with finite continuous graphs Γ=(V,E) whose edges are unit-length continuous intervals, equipped with the shortest-path metric on the underlying topological graph; that ambient setup is implicit in your draft and should be stated to make the question stand alone. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.14554))

The symbol G(Γ) should be named explicitly as the corresponding combinatorial graph on the same endpoint set V, and n should be defined explicitly as |V|. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.14554))

χ_{1/2}(Γ) is not just the size of a radius-1/2 ball cover: it is the minimum number c such that there exists a 1/2-cover by balls together with a colour assignment to those balls in which any two intersecting balls receive different colours. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.14554))

Section 3.3 intentionally restricts attention to r=1/2 because the authors regard that case as the direct continuous analogue of ordinary graph colouring; this restriction should be reflected explicitly. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.14554))

The paper asks first for bounds as functions of χ(G(Γ)) and n, and only secondarily asks about bounds in terms of other polynomial-time computable parameters; a refined version should preserve that ordering. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.14554))

The natural quantifier is for every finite continuous graph Γ, not only for the special complete or planar examples discussed earlier in the same section. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.14554))
refined_question: Let Γ=(V,E) be a finite continuous graph in the sense of Definitions 1–4, with unit-length continuous edges and shortest-path metric, let G(Γ) be its corresponding combinatorial graph on the same endpoint set V, and let n:=|V|. Define χ_{1/2}(Γ) to be the least integer c for which there exists a 1/2-cover B={B(p,1/2): p∈E} of Γ together with a colour map f:B→{1,…,c} such that f(B)≠f(B') whenever B∩B'≠∅. What general lower and upper bounds can be established for χ_{1/2}(Γ) as functions of χ(G(Γ)) and n, and, if stronger, as functions of other polynomial-time computable parameters of Γ or G(Γ)?
justification: This is the nearest paper-faithful formulation of your draft: it matches the exact open question at the end of Section 3.3 rather than the neighboring conjecture about Γ(K_n) or the planar-graph question. The refined wording imports the notation and hidden assumptions that the paper relies on nearby: Definitions 3 and 4 supply the model of a continuous graph and the correspondence Γ↔G(Γ), while Definition 11 and the surrounding discussion define χ_{1/2}(Γ) and explain why Section 3.3 fixes the radius to 1/2. ([arxiv.org](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2501.14554))
